I used these for air travel and they worked great. I changed my rating to five stars. These worked perfectly for canceling out the drone of the engine so I could easily hear movies or books on my iPad. The even helped to tone down the ear piercing screams of the child who cried nonstop for the ten hour flight. I'm so happy with these. For the price they are just outstanding.
*****
As I always do when I receive new ear buds I changed to the smallest ear tips. Normally that works well for me. I did that with these ear buds and they felt comfortable. I didn't think the noise cancelling was working correctly though. I tried using them while running the vacuum. I contacted the seller and they suggested changing to a different ear tip. The ear buds came with several sizes of regular foam ear tips and one additional "Comply Foam tips." I tried the Comply tips and they fit in my ear tightly. Today when I ran the vacuum with these tips I was able to listen to an audio book. I did have to turn up the volume a bit but not excessively. I tried turning off the noise cancelling feature and I couldn't hear the audio book at all. I bought these for upcoming air travel and I think they are going to work very well. Finally, I think they have excellent sound quality, both with the noise canceling turned off or on. I'm not an audiophile, I listen to some music but I use more often for audiobooks. They have a nice clean sound. I believe they're a good value for the money.

I’ve been using the converter for a few weeks and usually leave the small connector bit -- the oval piece -- plugged into my laptop even when I’m not charging it. It’s small enough that I don’t notice it.

The magnetic connection is reasonably strong, though the magnets could be stronger. The other bit, the part that plug into the charging cord, doesn’t always “click” on the first attempt.

I’m able to plug in other USB C cables, but my USB C to USB 3.0 adapters don’t fit.

Aside from those quibbles, I like this converter quite a bit. I’m even tempted to get another for the backup charger I have in my upstairs office, because I like having the safety and convenience of MagSafe so much.

Jabra Elite 65t Earbuds – Alexa Built-in, True Wireless Earbuds with Charging Case, Copper Black – Bluetooth Earbuds Engineered for The Best True Wireless Calls and Music Experience I agree with the other reviewer who said they look like hearing aids (before anyone jumps down my throat, nothing wrong with hearing aids, except that's not the look I'm going for, especially at this price point). I expected a much more light gold/pearl color earbud, and instead received an ugly flat ivory/gold pair and also look much larger in my ear than I had anticipated. As soon as I put them in, I thought to myself that they look like hearing aids, and when I saw the other person's Amazon review indicating the same, knew I wasn't crazy.

I tested them out for a bit and they were super easy to pair, sound quality seemed very good (compared to much less expensive wireless earbuds I have purchased on Amazon), and the button press controls seemed intuitive. However, I could tell they would become quite uncomfortable after extended periods of time. Not only are they large, but you have to press the buttons (especially on the left bud which controls volume and song skipping) pretty hard to get them to work, which presses them in to your ear even more, and that ends up hurting after a while. However, I will say that when I first put them in, they fit very snugly and I would not hesitate to use them for working out.

I am going to go with my first pick and try out the Samsung Galaxy Buds instead as they are supposed to have a sleeker profile than these. If I didn't already have the Galaxy Buds in mind, I would stick with the Jabras but go for the black color.

**EDIT 7/21/19**: I ended up buying the Samsung Galaxy Bud and enjoy them significantly more. Rather than buttons, they function by gestures (ie, tap once for play/pause, tap twice for next song/answer call, etc.), and you can customize what you want a long hold to do in the app that connects to the buds. In addition, they are smaller and have a much sleeker profile as I had expected!
text_fidelity_b: Jabra Elite 65t Earbuds – Alexa Built-in, True Wireless Earbuds with Charging Case, Copper Black – Bluetooth Earbuds Engineered for The Best True Wireless Calls and Music Experience

HP ENVY 13-13.99 Inches Thin Laptop w/ Fingerprint Reader, 4K Touchscreen, Intel Core i7-8565U, NVIDIA GeForce MX250 Graphics, 16GB SDRAM, 512GB SSD, Windows 10 Home (13-aq0044nr, Natural Silver) These are probably the last words that come to mind when thinking of a laptop, but this Ultrabook earns its name and then some in every way, because anyone who sees you using this will be BESIDE themselves, and I mean SICK, with Envy. This thang is FIYAH!!!!!!!!!!

Let's start with the unboxing: it arrives in a sleek, black box with a beautiful photo of the laptop on its cover, and when you open it, you are awed by the pristine, silver gleaming contraption inside. When you pick it up and gently unwrap it from its plastic film, you are wowed by how both light and elegant it is in your hands; how something so small can contain your life, and then you can't wait to start filling it up with it. You open the lid and lift the mesh cover protecting the keys; you notice the setup leaflet and take out the power cord, plug her in and turn her on.

From there, Cortana takes over, guiding you through the setup! By voice command! Very Jason Bourne. You set up your fingerprint log in, sign in to your accounts and then once everything is registered, off into the wild wild web you go. The first thing you'll notice is how FAST this baby is, the gentle whir of the machine as she takes you off to the farthest reaches of the world if you check out the 4K resolution by looking at the Planet Earth series. It's enough to bring tears to your eyes. You'll be mesmerized by the rhythmic clicking of the keys as you go to your favorite websites and download/install your must-have apps and programs; you will find yourself looking down at the keyboard and smiling as if you've been enchanted by a new lover, and you HAVE!

Fujifilm FinePix J40 12.2 MP Digital Camera with 3x Optical Zoom and 3-Inch LCD (Includes 2 GB SD Memory Card) The camera is $[..]for gosh sakes! It's an amazing little piece of technology. The 3X optics and 12.2MP CMOS camera are well matched in the optical train to provide a great image for casual photos adequate for most users. It's the simplest start-up I've ever seen. The viewer LCD provides a maximum size to the package. `The manual' is 7 steps of which 4 include inserting memory, battery, charging battery and turning it on. It's `point and shoot' in the extreme.

I work in the domain of optics & imaging design. My wife has a 5 year old Fuji camera of this same genre that I've gone to some lengths to compare with Nikon and Canon in this low cost market. Without getting technical ... for the old Fuji, there are no user discernable image quality differences. The Fuji optics were superior (i.e. best objective lens light capture and transfer). Take your pick between the 3 on the backend image processing system/PC interface.

My wife has carried the 5 year old Fuji in her purse every day ... that's a technically demanding reliability challenge. Fuji can be relied on to deliver the best value for money in an image capture platform if you're designing a million dollar platform or this $69 platform. You're not paying the premium for the huge advertisement budget of Nikon and Canon when you buy Fuji. I think you just get a better camera.

I can't speak to this unit's reliability for now. A 3x optical train with autofocus, f-stop, etc mechanisms and micro motors are robust to a point. They will all fail, even the highest dollar product, if exposed to the wrong environment (g-shock, sand, salt spray, thermal shock, etc).

text_fidelity_a:
Canon Office Products MG5420 Wireless Color Photo Printer with Scanner and Copier I've had problems with Pixmas in the past, mostly having to do with wireless networks and having to reinstall the software over and over to try to get them to hang on to network settings. I can't guarantee that this printer is going to be any better in the long run, but the set-up actually works pretty well if you use the standard version, not the WPS... and I'm getting way ahead of myself on this one.

To begin with, the printer requires a lot of time for set-up. You're not going to be doing this on the fly, so set aside an hour or so to: 1) remove all the tape of which there is much, 2) read over the instructions 3) install the ink, 4) run a print alignment 5) set up your wireless connection (about which more in a moment) 6) install the software (which takes a good 15 minutes or more), and 7) put the machine (and yourself) through its paces. Yeah, it's going to take a while.

Now I know you can read about the features on your own, so I'm here to tell you about the things that work for me and those that don't. First off, the wireless set-up is confusing. Choose Standard instead of WPS and save yourself some headaches unless you're a computer whiz kid. After the third error message in the WPS set-up I went to standard, entered my pass code and had the connection up and running in about a minute.

Once that was done and the software was installed I fired up the Canon Image Garden. First I scanned an image and attempted to rotate, crop and fix any deficiencies I found. The scan was over sharp and looked a bit jagged, but a little fiddling with the Canon software fixed that. Canon software also rotated and cropped perfectly. One really nice feature is that they remind you to put the printing side of the paper down in the paper cassette. How many pieces of paper will that save?

The biggest complaint I had was that it didn't give me a choice of which paper cassette to use for printing, so I got a ridiculously truncated image on the first try. I believe it chooses the paper based on the size of the image, which I get, but at the same time that limits flexibility in printing. I opened another photo processing program and it allowed me to print from whatever cassette I liked. Coupled with a better suite of applications for correction and enhancement, I think it's safe to say that I'll be using the Canon software almost never.

Printing on plain paper is clearly not going to be as satisfactory as it is on glossy, but in some cases I found it surprisingly good, good enough to give you an idea of what sort of image you're going to end up with when you switch to photo paper. It's also more than good enough for printing out emails and web pages.

Scanning and printing are both pretty fast, another plus. And the copy function works pretty seamlessly without any sort of computer interface. Just punch a couple of buttons and Bob's your uncle! It does take a bit of time to warm up and is a little noisy but no more so than any Canon printer I've ever used. It's not bothersome, in my opinion. You might feel otherwise.

Inks are easy to install, but you'll find refills pricey, no question. I suspect off-brand ones are available or will be soon enough.

In short, it's a good, inexpensive printer for a home or home office. Use photo paper and settings and get the full quality the MG5420 is capable of producing; I think it's pretty remarkable. The photos I printed out are as good as or in one case, better than the original. That's a powerful recommendation in my book.
text_fidelity_b: Canon Office Products MG5420 Wireless Color Photo Printer with Scanner and Copier

text_fidelity_a:
Nikon D3100 DSLR Camera with 18-55mm f/3.5-5.6 Auto Focus-S Nikkor Zoom Lens (Discontinued by Manufacturer) First, let me preface that I in NO way count myself a photog. I am just a shutter bug who has been firing frames almost non-stop since the age of 18. I learned on my dad's 'old' Nikon SLR with an f/1.2 lens. The Nikon SLRs/DSLRs I have owned are: N50, N60, N55, N80 and D50. My N50 ad N80 had the best lenses. The N60 and N55 were not as great and the D50 was a fabulous entry-level digital. The only medium format camera I own is my Holga. But hey, unlike the photographer at Portrait Innovations, at least I know 'medium format' does not refer to the number of megapixels at which I am shooting. As for my working knowledge, I had three semesters of photography in college. I can process/print both B&W and color film. (Not that that does me any good these days LOL) I can shoot completely 'manual' and I have stood among many pro photographers on the bridge at sunset, waiting for the color to be just right on Half Dome. (My Bogen tripod was way too heavy to be practical for an amateur but it gave me street credit.) So, in a nut shell, I shoot by the 'Sunny 16' rule. I know that opening my f-stop should increase my shutter speed give me a shorter depth of field; and, per the great Ansel Adams, f/8 is a proper exposure for all pictures.

That said, I hate my D3100.

I have had metering issues since I opened the box. I bought the camera so I could take 'even better' pictures of my infant son than I was getting from my D50. Ha. Joke was on me.

The contrast was BLINDING on the factory settings and every shot was over exposed. I have tried every metering option in the menu but the only changes I can achieve are under-exposure, blurred focus and missed shots. It's go high or go without.

I always lower my ISO to 100 when I'm outside because I crave rich color but it's just not there. I have tried Aperture Priority, Shutter Priority and Manual. Nothing. f/16 over my film speed on a sunny day. That's supposed to work! I have used it on many a 'less complicated' camera and achieved photos that make jaws drop. Well, there's no jaw dropping with this camera.

The metering overrides my manual choices every time. It's like I'm having a battle of wits with my camera. :( It reminds me of the days when Kodak was marketing 800-speed film as a universal, never-miss-a-shot solution to all your photo woes. Bleh. Just because there's always an image doesn't mean it's the RIGHT exposure.

I get that being an entry-level/made-for-the-masses DSLR really does mean it's a glorified point-and-shoot but it should preform at least as well as it's predecessors. Honestly, I got far more reliable results from my Canon SureShot and a roll of Kodak 100.

My expectation for a camera is that the image should be very close to perfect when the shutter closes. I know there's always room for improvement before printing but that's the art of photography. The hours I spend working on my photos after the shot should be to make them pop. Instead, my time is spent trying to rescue precious memories.

If you are considering this camera as your first DSLR because you think it will improve your skills, skip it. Invest in an equally expensive point-and-shoot that will give you all the same manual controls and preform much better in low-light situations. The D3100 does not live up to the standards of a Nikon SLR.

I gave it a second star because my son pulled mine off the counter about a year after I bought it and although the case cracked, it didn't seem to hurt the camera. Unfortunately, it impact didn't help it, either. (Yes, I was actually hopeful.)
text_fidelity_b: Nikon D3100 DSLR Camera with 18-55mm f/3.5-5.6 Auto Focus-S Nikkor Zoom Lens (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

Western Digital 320GB WD Black Performance Mobile Hard Drive - 7200 RPM Class, SATA 6 Gb/s, , 32 MB Cache, 2.5" - WD3200LPLX Update 8-7-19: I went to the WD website to register my two drives. They show as no warranty from WD, presumably because they were bought through a reseller. Just so you know ...

I use these as primary storage (and backup storage) for our MacBook Air laptop. Most MacBooks now come with solid state drives, meaning memory chip based drives, not physical spinning disks. They are much more expensive than the heritage physical disk approach, such that the largest SSD that we could get with our 2017 MacBook Air was a 256 GB drive. These WD Black (virtually enterprise level) drives are 500 GB each, so our storage is 2x that of the built in drive. We use one as our primary external drive; once a month we install the 2nd drive (also externally), copy the files across, and put it into our safe deposit box at the bank. If we ever lose a drive, whether to failure or someone breaking in and stealing our drive and laptop, we're only 30 days behind, a real advantage.

The only downside to this drive is that the warranty on the drive itself is provided by the Seller, OEMGENUINE. The drive came marked with a label on the drive as a Seller 5 year warranty, with no terms provided. The downside risk is there is no published warranty, either by the Seller or by WD on their website, and whatever warranty is provided is subject to the Seller still being in existence over the next 5 years. However, given the price of the drive ($35 or so), it was a reasonable risk to take, especially since we acquired two and use one as the backup to the primary one. The odds of losing two drives at the same time is pretty remote. So we accepted the risk, but dropped the review for the product & seller by 1 star. If you go to the WD website, they do claim a 5 year limited warranty. I am a little surprised that the WD website doesn't provide a link to their warranty. So if we can't reach OEMGENUINE should we have a problem, I'm not sure what protection we'll have from WD. Something to consider if that's important to you.

These are fast drives (7200 rpm for the 500GB drive), which is noticeably faster than the previous bulk drives we've purchased online and/or removed from existing systems, which have all been 5400 rpm drives. SATA compatible, plug and play, no issues yet but it's only been a few days. If something materially changes, I'll post an update.
text_fidelity_b: Western Digital 320GB WD Black Performance Mobile Hard Drive - 7200 RPM Class, SATA 6 Gb/s, , 32 MB Cache, 2.5" - WD3200LPLX

text_fidelity_a:
Large Print Backlit Keyboard, Quiet USB Wired Computer Keyboard, Full Size Keyboard with White Illuminated LED Compatible for Windows Desktop, Laptop, PC, Gaming, Black UPDATE: I'm changing my rating from 5 stars to 2 stars due to a rather quick failure of this keyboard. After only about 2 weeks use, some keys are non-functional (such as num lock -- it no longer works at all) and other keys are acting up (double entry when only pressed once). While the large labels and backlight design are great, the poor reliability, even for the low price, makes this a 2 star keyboard.

ORIGINAL REVIEW: This is an ideal keyboard if you find yourself squinting a bit to read key labels. The labels for each key on this keyboard are very large -- the largest I've come across. Additionally, it's backlit, allowing the labels to jump out even more.

The key action is decent. It's a bit clacky, but I've not had any issues with keys not properly registering. The backlight can be turned on and off with a single key. It also provides a number of useful shortcut function keys (accessed by pressing FN first, then the function key) such as vol up/down, play, mute, calculator, home page and others. I tend to not use them much (other than the Homepage and mute keys) but it's nice to have them be available.

It's plug and play compatible with Win 10. I plugged in the USB cord, Win 10 recognized it, and it was installed and ready to go.

The build quality is fine for a home keyboard but it lacks the durability for an office setting. Additionally, the backlight is not perfectly even (brighter at the base of the keyboard than the top). While these build quality issues puts my overall score at 4.5 stars, I'll round up since it does deliver its main benefit -- large, easy to read keys -- better than any other keyboard I've come across. Good value for the price.
text_fidelity_b: Large Print Backlit Keyboard, Quiet USB Wired Computer Keyboard, Full Size Keyboard with White Illuminated LED Compatible for Windows Desktop, Laptop, PC, Gaming, Black

While I didn't get to test out the USB 3.0 function of this card reader, it worked great on my regular USB 2.0 connections and speedily transferred over 500 photos in just a couple of minutes.

The only criticism I have of this card reader is that the profile is thick enough that on my computer, where I have two USB ports stacked one on top of another, I need to unplug something in order to be able to plug in this card reader. This isn't a big deal, since I have little USB extension cords that I can use if I truly don't want to unplug something else, but if the manufacturers are listening, I'd love to see a slimmer profile on any future models.

text_fidelity_a:
Sennheiser Momentum Headphone - Brown I am so very pleased with these headphones. I was expecting them to sound pretty good given the Sennheiser lineage, but they really set me back on my heels with the sound quality, comfort, and overall design.

Let's start with the easy one - how they look. To my eye, they are very nicely styled. Classic-looking rather than flashy. I especially like how the headband is not excessively padded -- it does not stick out when you wear them. Very elegant overall. Everything looks and feels high quality.

They also hit the mark regarding comfort. I usually have a 1 hour limit when it comes to over-the-ear headphones, in that after an hour of wearing them I've reached my limit of tolerance. These, however, felt wonderful. They are light enough that I hardly noticed the weight. More importantly, the ear cups fit me just right. Cushy enough to seal out ambient noise but not at the expense of having my ears feel like they were trapped in a vice. They felt just as good well into hour 2 as they did in the first 15 minutes. I found the headband also very comfortable for long stretches without getting "sweaty head" as I get with other headphones.

But it's the sound that counts. To my ear, these `phones deliver in spades. I started off with some Stanley Clarke. Wonderful -- ample bass but not at the expense of hearing every string being plucked. I listened to School Days a couple of times in a row, just amazed at how good it sounded. The same for Florence and the Machine -- solid, deep bass but not overwhelming.

Next up was Metric to see how vocals come through. Again, superb. I was finally able to figure out some of the lyrics on Synthetica that never came through clear enough on my ear buds. Regina Spektor was also an absolute pleasure to listen to and have all facets of her unique vocal styling come through so clearly.

I also tried them for movie watching on my Fire, and again was very pleased. Dialog was clean and pronounced; explosions were, well, explosive.

The noise isolation is quite good. These are not noise cancelling headphones, so some ambient noise will leak in, but it keeps out everything other than the most significant ambient sounds.

I really can't fault these on any criterion. They look great, feel great, and sound great. Granted, the price is not so great, but good quality costs. If you're a demanding headphone user, these are worth the money charged. Highly recommend.
text_fidelity_b: Sennheiser Momentum Headphone - Brown

I had this product suggested to me by a friend who was using it for two screens with our work laptop and it seemed to be working fine. I only used it for one screen in the beginning and the very first thing I noticed with it was that it would become very warm or hot to the touch after less than an hour. I used it for a few months and the next thing it did was cause my mouse and screens to lag behind during operation. I then purchased a camera that I tried to plug into this docking station and everything went even more haywire with the camera, mouse and screens both acting up when operating my laptop, and of course the device was always warm to hot. So, I stopped using it and just direct wired everything to my laptop, which is extremely inconvenient when I need to move my laptop around, and I don't have enough ports to plug things in. Then, my husband bought a new CPU and needed to plug his two screens in so I let him try this docking station, and it wouldn't even register with the CPU at all. I plugged it back into my laptop where I knew it did work at one time, and sure enough, it doesn't work anymore.

So, basically it didn't function the way it should have, and within 6 months it just stopped working all together. Biggest waste of money, and now I can't return it.

text_fidelity_a:
TOZO T6 True Wireless Earbuds Bluetooth 5.3 Headphones Touch Control with Wireless Charging Case IPX8 Waterproof Stereo Earphones in-Ear Built-in Mic Headset Premium Deep Bass White (2022 Upgraded) I just got the TOZO T6 waterproof headphones tonight. One of the main reasons I picked them is because they were same day delivery for me. Since my skullcandy wireless earbuds had ticked me off for the last time I was ready to find something new. I am so happy to say that so far I am not disappointed.

First of all, the packaging was immaculate. The unboxing experience felt like I was unboxing a new phone. Everything was packaged so neatly and purposefully.

Fit - There is a wider availability of earbud sizes than any other headphones I have ever gotten. Not just in girth, but also depth, so there is an option for people who may have a more shallow ear canal. Very thoughtful. As soon as I paired the earbuds and picked the appropriate sized silicone earbud tip I put them in. They were lighter and fit more ergonomically than my skullcandy did. They are smaller and fit my ear more comfortably.

Pairing - the process as simple as pulling the earbuds out of the box, taking the plastic tabs off, putting them in the charging case, taking them out of the charging case and waiting for the colored lights to begin flashing blue and red (took about 6 seconds). Then I scanned for TOZO 6 under "bluetooth settings" on my phone. It was literally the simplest pairing experience I've ever had. Especially considering I nearly returned my skullcandy earbuds after over an hour and them not showing up on my phone when I scanned. This was pleasantly simple and the directions given actually worked as they were supposed to.

The sound - I didn't do any adjustments to the sound on my phone, other than volume and the sound was crisp, it was full bodied, clearly hearing bass, and even the highest notes in clarity. I had the volume of the song I was listening to at a bit less than 50% and full sound that didn't allow normal room noises to infiltrate. I even knocked quite hard on my wooden nightstand to test this and I could not hear the knocking.

There is the option to alternate which earbud is first or secondary. Just turn off the one you want to be secondary and the other will remain primary when you turn the other back on again. I appreciate that either earbud can be primary or secondary or that can be used one at a time as well.

Phone call clarity. I was able to hear crisp clear sound while on the phone and the person I talked to said I sounded crisp and clear as well.

Charge - the earbud case is able to charge on a charging platform or with a micro-USB charging cable (included.) This was the only disappointment I encountered as I would have liked the T6 case to a accept the same USB C cable that my Galaxy Note phone uses. That is a minor thing that would not make me not want to use these earbuds.

There were several colors to choose from, black, white, light blue, mint green, purple and pink. I chose the light blue since it matches my current phone case. However, if ever after your purchase you tire of the color of your case, there are silicone charger cases available on Amazon for purchase specifically for the TOZO T6 charger case. This can allow your earbud case to be conveniently hooked to a bag or belt loop.

I cannot vouch for battery life yet, since I have only had them a couple of hours. I've had them in my ears for about 1.5 hours and they are still reading at 100%. So I am giving it 5⭐ for now.

Over all well worth the $39.99 I paid for these. I'm so happy with my purchase.
text_fidelity_b: TOZO T6 True Wireless Earbuds Bluetooth 5.3 Headphones Touch Control with Wireless Charging Case IPX8 Waterproof Stereo Earphones in-Ear Built-in Mic Headset Premium Deep Bass White (2022 Upgraded)

Canon Powershot S2 IS 5MP Digital Camera with 12x Optical Image Stabilized Zoom (OLD MODEL) I have only had this camera a few weeks but it has met all my expectations--I got it to photograph jewelry and small artwork primarily, at which it excels. I am also am finding it does a great job on a lot of other kinds of shots. I find I enjoy photographing birds--a tough subject--and have gotten some nice shots of them with this camera. The controls are easy to operate, conveniently located, and pretty easy to figure out even without resorting to the manual. I'm still doing a lot of experimenting with different settings to "learn" the camera's capabilities and get a feel for its sensitivity to light and its optics...an exercise highly recommended for folks like me who are new to cameras with manual controls. Have taken a few video clips with it that came out great.

The memory card it came with is kind of a joke--I bought a Kingston 2 GB card to use instead and have been real happy with that. It writes super-fast and I come nowhere close to ever running out of room (but I delete a lot of shots, too). Also, rechargeable batteries are HIGHLY recommended. I have three sets...one set lasted for three weeks of casual use--even with the LCD often open.

I've added a 52mm adapter tube and a few filters, plus a hood. Mainly I wanted the adapter and a UV filter to protect the lens for tight super-macro shots. One of these days I might get a wide angle lens. If you're going to be doing macro stuff or using the zoom a lot, use of a tripod will be key in getting clearly focused shots.
text_fidelity_b: Canon Powershot S2 IS 5MP Digital Camera with 12x Optical Image Stabilized Zoom (OLD MODEL)

text_fidelity_a:
RCA BRC10GR Bathroom Clock Radio (Green) Updated review:

I've become somewhat dependent on the sight of this bright blue radio. Every morning I stumble, groggy-eyed, into my bathroom. Having this clear-sounding radio, blasting my favorite music, is a nice pick-me-up as I shower. But does the design offer me anything more than what I would expect from a typical shower radio?

PROS: It's cleverly designed to mimic the shape of a shampoo. It melds easily into the background. My initial fear was that I would accidentally grab it instead of the real thing, but so far that hasn't happened.

PROS: The sound quality is tinny but quite decent for a shower radio.

PROS: The radio offers a "store" function where you can bookmark your favorite radio stations and get to them fast by using a "recall" button. This is a feature common to most clock radios but I don't spend enough time in the bathroom to use it. I basically stick to one station while showering and can't see myself using the "store" function unless I'm taking a long bath. Still, nice to have that option.

PROS: Great battery life! I used my AA batteries for this and it has been running for months with no problem.

CONS: It's not that easy to see the buttons. They're located on the sides of the device but the positions are not intuitive. I always have to squint a little to see the print above the buttons because the buttons do not stick out.

CONS: "Light up" function. The time display is very clear and easy to read as-is. Since it's not a bedtime clock radio that benefits from having a glow-in-the-dark function, this feature feels extraneous to me. Perhaps it's best for someone who likes to take a bath with candles all around.

CONS: Not space saving. I used to have a shower radio that could be hooked over the showerhead. While the radio is not huge, I still had to move my shampoo and conditioner bottles to make room for it.

Overall it is a decent radio and I have been using it since I got it with no problems.
text_fidelity_b: RCA BRC10GR Bathroom Clock Radio (Green)

The super-long cord is also not fun because I find myself constantly managing it to ensure it doesn't get tangled. In contrast, Sony's over-the-should "OFC neckchain" design in the previous version coupled with the modular approach they took to the cord - approx. 1 foot with an optional 3 foot extension - meant that I could clip the previous iPod on the inside of my coat and be unconstrained by a long cord. Ultimately, the whole idea of a remote that is integrated into the cord feels like a misfire to me. The 2G generation iPod Shuffle plus the older generation of Sony earbuds are far more functional and I'm going back for as long as my old Shuffle will hold out.

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech G502 Proteus Spectrum RGB Tunable Gaming Mouse, 12,000 DPI On-The-Fly DPI Shifting, Personalized Weight and Balance Tuning with (5) 3.6g Weights, 11 Programmable Buttons I’m not a hardcore gamer anymore, so for the past few years, I’ve been using a Logitech M570 Wireless Trackball (thumb trackball). I like trackballs for everyday use, and it’s adequate for casual World of Warcraft playing. Most of the time I just futz around leveling alts or doing 5 mans with friends.

But lately I’ve been wanting a mouse I can customize, with more options to adjust my playstyle. It’s cold in my house in the winter, so I wanted to set up mouseover macros and use more mouse buttons, because my hands are cold sitting on the keyboard. So the G502 Proteus Spectrum seemed like a good mouse to review.

I just had one problem: my computer can’t customize the mouse. Why? I have a Mac Book Air.

Now, I know the G502 says on the box that it supports Windows. There’s no mention of Mac support. But I’ve never had a problem with my Mac recognizing Logitech mice, so I figured I’d be safe. What I didn’t know is that Logitech gaming mice have separate software from the Logitech Control Center for regular Logitech mice.

After some Googling, I found the Logitech Gaming Software, which supports Mac OS X 10.8.x and up. I installed it on a Mavericks machine and a Yosemite machine. Neither computer’s Logitech Gaming Software was able to find the mouse. The G502 Proteus CORE is supported, but not the G502 Proteus SPECTRUM.

So right now, I’m unable to customize any of the extra buttons or RGB lighting or any of the other special features. It’s a really fancy basic mouse. I will continue to check for Proteus Spectrum support in the Mac Logitech Gaming Center, and update this review when I can customize things. I’m going into so much detail on the Mac side of things because I know I’m not the only Mac person who tried to use this mouse. I think there’s a workaround with Bootcamp or using a Windows computer, but I’m unable to try that.

I did use the mouse for a few weeks, to test the comfort. I’m really picky on how mice feel in my hand. I’m female and have smaller hands. I like how this mouse didn’t feel too short, and it wasn’t too heavy or wide for me to use comfortably for hours at a time. I also liked the included weights, so you can adjust the weight of the mouse. I haven’t had a mouse with an adjustable weight before, and I liked that extra level of customization.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech G502 Proteus Spectrum RGB Tunable Gaming Mouse, 12,000 DPI On-The-Fly DPI Shifting, Personalized Weight and Balance Tuning with (5) 3.6g Weights, 11 Programmable Buttons

Polk Audio Atrium 6 Outdoor Speakers with Bass Reflex Enclosure (Pair, Black) - All-Weather Durability | Broad Sound Coverage | Speed-Lock Mounting System The Good:
-They sound good. They're not audiophile speakers, of course, but they sound much better than some of the other outdoor speakers I've heard, and better than any other outdoor speaker I auditioned in this price range.
-They're rugged, which you really need in an outdoor speaker. It's not just rain, after all; an outdoor speaker has to contend with errant footballs, rough handling, curious animals, etc, any of which would break a normal indoor speaker. These have a metal grill and very sturdy build and should stand up to almost anything.
-I like the mounting system; very flexible and well-engineered.

The Bad (and these are minor)
-Very cramped, awkward space for the binding posts. I use banana plugs because I need a quick, easy way to hook them up (standing on a ladder, fumbling around behind the speaker) and there's not enough room back there for normal banana plugs. I wound up buying some right-angle plugs (I got the Monoprice), and those resolved this for me.
-Sound quality is good for an outdoor speaker in this price range but if you don't need a rugged speaker, you can get much better sound for the price. As I'm writing this review, the ELAC Debut 2.0 B6.2 is on sale for about the same price as these Atriums, and the ELAC has much better sound. Of course, the ELAC probably wouldn't survive a night on my patio.

Bottom line: If you need an outdoor speaker in this price range, this speaker would be my recommendation.
text_fidelity_b: Polk Audio Atrium 6 Outdoor Speakers with Bass Reflex Enclosure (Pair, Black) - All-Weather Durability | Broad Sound Coverage | Speed-Lock Mounting System

SanDisk Ultra Fit 128GB USB 3.0 Flash Drive - SDCZ43-128G-GAM46 It just landed in the return envelope today... There has been three major things that led to this:
1) The Vault software stopped responding and started crashing every time I tried to run it. Data inside it were obviously inaccessible. So...
2) I decided to make it brand new and reformat the drive. Using just Windows explorer it did not work (refused), then using disk management - no success, finally using prompt and unconditional formatting (both full and quick) would end up in reporting that disk is not accessible - apparently there is writing protection on it that I could not get passed and it would not allow me to reformat it. So...
3) After attempting to reformat the disk became unreadable and Windows could not see it (disk management would see it as raw partition, not able to format it). Next, I took it off the USB port in order to reinsert it and then I almost burned my finger! This thing was so HOT I could fry an egg on it, if it was bigger! After reinserting into the USB port it would still be unrecognizable.
In short, the disk became a small brick and landed in the return envelope.
Avoid SanDisk as they apparently shovel the write protection down your throat and you can't do anything with your drive later on. So much for your customer flexibility with your product. Rather pick a very similar, ultra-small Samsung USB drive of the same size, also available from Amazon. That one comes clean (i.e. no imposed software nor writing protection) and apparently does not heat at all, or very little compared to this little oven.
text_fidelity_b: SanDisk Ultra Fit 128GB USB 3.0 Flash Drive - SDCZ43-128G-GAM46

Bose Wave Music System IV ,Auxiliary- Espresso Black I have been using a Bose Wave Radio for many years and it has always provided me with great, reliable sound whether with a CD, radio, or through my ipod.

This newest model is a bit more streamlined, takes up the same amount of space, and has no visible buttons. The remote is intuitive and easy to set up and navigate.

I hooked up my ipod with a 3.5 male to male cable and it worked beautifully.

The sound quality, whether listening to Janos Starker on cello, Mozart, Kirtan (yoga chants), Enya, harpsichord, synthesizer, or spoken word, was rich, full-bodied, layered, and balanced. Regardless of whether the decibel level was low or high, though the high range was fantastic.

As they instructed, I placed the system a couple of feet from the wall, not in a corner. It filled the room evenly and fully.

You might think this is a lot of money for "a radio," but it is far more than a radio, and may outlast you. Once you get used to the great sound other less expensive offerings sound thin, tinny, and electronic.

If you are looking for something that will sound just as good 15 years after you bought it, I would recommend a Bose radio. I thought my first one was a fortune, but if I reflect on how many thousands of times I have enjoyed listening to it, and the pennies it cost me a day, it has been fully amortized.

text_fidelity_a:
Acer Aspire R 15 2-in-1 Laptop, 15.6" Full HD Touch, 7th Gen Intel Core i7, GeForce 940MX, 12GB DDR4, 256GB SSD, R5-571TG-7229 This will be a fairly detailed and honest review.

1. Who is this for?
This computer is what I would consider a gateway computer. Those who are looking at upgrading a fairly old or not so powerful laptop and are looking to do a little more productivity, this is a great option.

2. What do you get?
Well you can probably read the description, however it's worth noting. You get an Intel i7 7500u CPU (dual core with 4 threads) 12gb DDR4 RAM, Nvidia 940mx GPU, a 256gb SSD, 15.6" 1080p screen, fingerprint reader, and a backlit keyboard.

The reason I mention all of the feautures is because you would be hardpressed to find another laptop with these features for the same price. To my knowledge there is not laptop on the market for $800 with an i7, dedicated graphics, 12gb of RAM and an SSD. This is really one of the best values on the market right now.

With all of that said, this isn't for everyone. If you want to do extensive gaming, this is not for you. Can it game? Yes, light gaming can be achieved, however it isn't marketed as a gaming laptop. Is this for someone who wants to do editing (video, audio, photos)? Yes, again light editing can be achieved.

What blew me away with this computer is the speakers! They are fantastic! I usually use headphones and would consider myself somewhat picky with sound, and for laptop speakers these are really something great.

This computer is really a middle of the pack all arounders dream. If you dabble in a little of this and a little of that but don't do anything professionally or extremely serious, this is really all you need.

Also, everyone's experience is different. Some hate loud fans, and if this is pushed the fans will be audible. Some don't like that the backlit keyboard times out after 30 seconds of no use. These things really don't bother me.

Lastly, the versatility of this laptop is really great. I've bought tablets and sold them because I couldn't justify having a laptop and tablet, then bought tablets again because I missed the things I could do with them that I was missing on a laptop. This solved all of those issues except size. It's pretty big, which for some is a plus others its not.

Overall, if you are looking at upgrading and don't want to spend $1,200-2,000 on a flagship model laptop this is a great option! I can't recommend this enough.

text_fidelity_a:
FiiO X5 High Resolution Music Player (2nd Generation)(Titanium) I love my FiiO X5 2nd gen player! I love that it has two micro SD card slots (which I use both for a total of 192GB of storage space, with one 64GB card and one 128GB card), because I can put two separate sets of music in there and go back and forth between the cards depending on my musical needs (for example, on the 64GB card, I put recently purchased tracks, and for the entirety of my rest of my library, I put those tracks on the 128GB card). It allows me faster access to my newer stuff, which I want to listen to now, vs. randomizing the rest of my music from the other card.

The sound is unheard of (ha ha, sorry for the pun). Nothing compares to the quality of sound that comes out of this little machine, for its size and price. Pair it with a set of high quality hi-fi headphones and some FLAC music files, and you've got yourself an insane little music machine. You'll never go back to Apple or another brand of music player. You'll find yourself hooking it up to your home sound system and playing all of your music through it. I can't say enough for the sound quality. You WILL notice a difference between crummy .mp3 files and other low-quality sound files. You WILL find yourself craving FLAC files, and you will go wherever you can to find them. You might even start converting your entire CD music collection into FLAC, even though you'd already converted them all to .mp3. You WILL find yourself hoping that someday soon, Amazon will start offering FLAC files instead of .mp3s! (HINT HINT NUDGE NUDGE!) ;) Seriously, though, you probably haven't realized how GOOD your music will sound until you listen to it on this FiiO X5 2nd gen. Even the .mp3s sound better. Especially if you use noise cancelling headphones.

I like that you can adjust the configuration and tell it which buttons to remain active when the screen is off, depending on your preferences. I also like that there are several preset themes to choose from. The screen is easy to read and nicely displays album art.

The unit itself has a wonderful weight to it given the aluminum shell. The volume wheel moves easily and there is a slight tactile feedback click. That wheel controls both the song volume and song selection, depending on which screen you're on when you use it. The power on button has a tiny LED light that's blue when it's running and red when it's charging. There are volume up/down buttons beneath the power button and those buttons are some of the buttons that you can choose whether or not to have active while the screen is off.

I'm not sure if I there's a firmware update that needs to be done that could change this, but there are a couple of things that are pretty bothersome in general about this unit:

1) There is no way to search for a song. If, like me, you have more than 5,000 songs, it's impossible to sit and scroll through each album/folder to find a specific song. I suppose if you're some kind of major organization guru (which I thought I was, but apparently not at this), it would be possible to arrange your music folders into genres or some other category to make it easier to get to the exact music you need to play, but if you've moved over from iTunes like I have, you're probably real spoiled with the ability to view songs either by artist, album, song name, etc., as well as the ability to do a search. Here, you're pretty much on your own, depending on how you've got your music library set up. Having purchased most of my music here on Amazon, it's all arranged by artist name in individual folders. I have several hundred folders set up like this, and scrolling through everything with that scroll wheel can take a very, very long time to find the one thing you're looking for.

2) The unit can be quite SLOW to respond to your clicks. It is not touch-screen, and when you click on a button to change tracks forward/backward or to change from looking at what's playing into another option, such as a list of the songs on the album, it can be quite sluggish. Again, if you're used to using an iPod, you'll be frustrated with the lack of responsiveness of this unit. Again, I keep hoping a firmware update will come out that addresses this.

3) Whenever you add music to your micro SD card(s) [NOTE: There is NO onboard storage, it's purely on whatever card(s) you insert into it] you have to completely update your whole media library. This can take a long time depending on how much music you have, so keep this in mind and don't expect to add music and listen to it immediately. In other words, plan ahead for this :)

4) It's not as user friendly as the typical Apple products you may be used to. You'll get used to it, but don't expect the polished feel because of issues like #1 and #2, above.

5) Playlists are not straightforward. Yes, you can be playing a song and add it to a playlist that resides on one of your SD cards. However, importing playlists can be tricky and you may find yourself looking to the internet to help convert your existing playlists from your prior player. Expect to spend some time on this unless you're totally okay with starting over from scratch (I wasn't okay with this). Also, any playlists that you save to your SD card that you've hand-converted do not show up as a playlist on the FiiO. Instead, you have to navigate to the file on your player as if you were looking for a song, and play it as if you were playing a song. Only playlists you've created on the machine show up in the Playlist section, not playlists you've brought in from elsewhere. There is no 'import' feature or anything fancy like that, so you're pretty much on your own unless you add a song one at a time to Playlist 1, Playlist 2, etc. (I do not yet see a way to rename these as there is no keyboard function on this machine, so you're stuck with those names).

I think with time, the FiiO's software will catch up closer to what you're seeing from the high-visibility media consumer based music players, but right now with this X5 you should be more concerned with how WONDERFUL your music sounds vs the issues associated with the frumpy software that comes with it.
text_fidelity_b: FiiO X5 High Resolution Music Player (2nd Generation)(Titanium)

text_fidelity_a:
ASUS VS197D-P 18.5" WXGA 1366x768 VGA Back-lit LED Monitor, Black I'm very pleased with this monitor. I needed to replace my second screen and didn't want to spend a lot, but needed a monitor with 1920x1200 resolution. This seemed like a decent bet. It has exceeded my expectations with regard to performance. The clarity is excellent -- it rivals my primary screen which cost three times as much!

The monitor is very lightweight. It comes with both DVI and VGA cables, which was unexpected. I like that there's no power transformer or wall wart. It has just a regular power cord. Set up is simple (just attached the base and no tools are needed).

Of course, at this price point some features are not present. For example, while the screen can be tilted back and forth a bit, it does not have any up/down adjustment, nor can it be swiveled into portrait mode. There's no USB connectors and no speakers. But for me, none of those were deal breakers. I wanted a good quality monitor that was affordable, and this hit the mark 100%. Plus, it does not scrimp on connections. There's DVI, VGA and HDMI. I'm using DVI at present since the PC I'm using it with is a few years old. But, my next PC will probably have a HDMI connection, making this monitor future-proof (well, as future-proof as any tech product can be).

If you're looking for a basic monitor that does not scrimp on image quality, this should definitely be on your short list. Also, check Amazon Warehouse for used ones. I got mine there (it was probably a customer's return). It looks brand new, and only ran me $127.
text_fidelity_b: ASUS VS197D-P 18.5" WXGA 1366x768 VGA Back-lit LED Monitor, Black

text_fidelity_a:
Acme Made Skinny Sleeve Medium (Stretchshell Neoprene) Sapphire/Grey AM10341 So... based on the product description, one can assume that any laptop that runs about 13"-14" should fit neatly into this sleeve. Well, not so much, really. When it arrives you'll see that the tag clearly states that it is for the Macbook Pro/Air 13. Nothing else. No Inspirons, no Yogas, and really not my Alienware 13. Oh, I can squeeze it into the sleeve if I work at it, and if I take the plastic insert out, but it's a lot like trying to fit into your skinny jeans after a weekend of Netflix and ice cream. You can do it, but it's not going to be pretty. And unfortunately getting my laptop back out of the sleeve was even harder. I checked the seams after two insertions and removals, and while they look fine now, I fear that repeated use might be hard on them.

So does it protect my laptop? Well, yes and no. It's in there pretty tightly, so the protective layer is stretched thin. And the end sticks out. I simply can't get it all the way into the sleeve. There's maybe a quarter to half an inch that protrudes. Now if I was tossing this into a briefcase or backpack, I wouldn't worry, but as it is, it's still vulnerable to being dropped along that edge or to being rained on or spilled on.

So overall what I would tell you is this: If you don't have a Macbook Pro/Air 13, then compare the measurements of your laptop to those of that model. If you're not close, look elsewhere.
text_fidelity_b: Acme Made Skinny Sleeve Medium (Stretchshell Neoprene) Sapphire/Grey AM10341

text_fidelity_a: Amazon Kindle Paperwhite Leather Case, Onyx Black - fits all Paperwhite generations prior to 2018 (Will not fit All-new Paperwhite 10th generation) After being a NOOK user for just over a year, I fell in love with the Kindle Paperwhite, decided to switch platforms, and joined the Kindle family in February. After using the Kindle for about a week without a cover, I felt I needed to protect my new device. I bought two cases from third party vendors, and they were just okay. My Paperwhite seemed to float around inside these cases, so I bit the bullet and bought Amazon's leather cover in Fuchsia. When I received it, I wasn't thrilled with the color, so I returned it and got Onyx Black instead. While I love it--it's very stylish, elegant, and the border blends perfectly with the device--my Kindle also kept blending in with other tech gadgets around the house that live in black cases. I went to Best Buy and looked at the case in Royal Purple (in my area, they only sell Onyx Black, Fuchsia, and Royal Purple), but again I didn't care for that color either. On a whim, I ordered the Persimmon case, which I got yesterday. I'm very happy!!! It is a beautiful coral color, not what the Amazon website depicts, but also not a true red, and the trim accentuates the Kindle perfectly. I don't find it distracting. I have been so happy with this case that I paid the extra $20 to turn off Special Offers and it works as advertised. The Kindle sits perfectly flush inside, closes flush, and even when I fold the front cover back there's no floating (very distracting when you're reading and the Kindle "shifts" when you move your finger to turn a page). Anyway, I'll be selling the Onyx Black case, which is, after one month of use, in excellent condition. I highly, highly recommend these cases for the Kindle Paperwhite, and if you like cheerful, bright colors, go with Persimmon. The only cons I can think of are: there should have been a teal and green option, and I wish the inside of the front cover had the Kindle logo engraved on it (don't think that's a lot to ask for the price; instead the inside logo feels like it was ironed on).
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Kindle Paperwhite Leather Case, Onyx Black - fits all Paperwhite generations prior to 2018 (Will not fit All-new Paperwhite 10th generation)

text_fidelity_a:
Tile - (Gen 1) - 1 Pack - Discontinued by Manufacturer The Tile system isn't perfect but it works (mostly) and to date I haven't run across any better options. So bearing in mind your needs and the device's limitations, it's probably worth getting (at the time of this writing) if you have things you're worried about misplacing.

Pros:

- EASY setup. The time it takes to send an eMail and receive a reply, and a few seconds more. I have heard people say it requires iPhone 4 and up - I have a 5 and everything was a breeze. I didn't use the picture feature initially but it was no problem to update later.

- Decent map feature - good enough to get you in general range of the FIND radius.

- An audible FIND jingle. Just loud enough to hear through a wallet. Louder sure would be better, but it has a tinny high-pitched jingle that's easy to identify once you've heard it.

- It's small enough to fit in my wallet. It's a bit bulky, but it does.

- It's weatherproof and sealed. I haven't actually tested that and don't want to, but it's a nice feature.

- On-phone settings are easy to operate, and allow you to turn off Bluetooth tracking without turning off the iPhone's Bluetooth.

- Easy to assign to other objects as needed (if you don't use the stick pad.) It has a hole, so you don't HAVE to stick it to anything permanently.

- Can add other users (beforehand, of course!)

- It works. The battery is only supposed to last about a year, though (we'll see!)

Cons:

- Bulkier than I thought - not quite as thick as a pen, but almost. About a half-dollar size.

- The FIND process takes a minute or two to adjust and is a little confusing at first.

- The FIND radius sure isn't perfectly accurate. But hey, it's something!

- Battery not replaceable. The Tile people will recycle it for you for a fee, but I doubt that is a rapid process.

I really like it. I don't lose stuff that often, but this is an awfully convenient tracking option - having a general idea is a LOT better than having NO idea at all! And I LOVE the idea of the Tile community! The Tile gives me peace of mind taking things through airports etc. If there's something you think you MIGHT mislay, I think the Tile is worth it.
text_fidelity_b: Tile - (Gen 1) - 1 Pack - Discontinued by Manufacturer

text_fidelity_a:
Securifi Almond - (3 Minute Setup) Touchscreen Wireless Router/Range Extender The tech geek in our household kept telling me there was nothing we could do to improve on the truly horrendous wireless internet service we have. He said we were stuck with the ISP we have and with their router (which he has in the far back bedroom, on the other side of our apartment from the pricey smart TV I haven't been able to use for anything but watching cable news). I haven't been able to stream anything from Amazon Prime, nor can I access the internet at all through the TV. So in complete frustration, without telling him, I ordered the Securifi Almond. Price was one factor in my decision, but I knew I wasn't going to be able to depend on him to help me set anything up and I'm not all that tech savvy.

One of the attractive selling points of this router is that it can be used either as a router or as a range extender. I planned to set it up as a range extender to see if I could get a better signal near my TV, but also had in mind that I might be able to persuade a certain somebody to try it as our router in place of the one that I feel like is defective (or just crummy) from our ISP.

I set it up myself. I just followed the installation on screen, and it was a snap. Fortunately, I knew what our log-in info was for our network so I didn't have to ask for help. I wasn't sure how it was supposed to work with the ethernet cable, so I plugged the Almond into the LAN port of of my TV and into one of the ports with a TV icon on the router. Then I tested it. Wow. The streaming is so much better than it was that I signed up for Netflix and started binging on "House of Cards." I still have the rotating download timer come up once or twice during an episode, but it gets done pretty quickly and the episode finishes playing. Before, I couldn't even load an episode or, worse, it would play a minute then completely drop the connection to the internet.

So I'm quite happy. This is a sleek little baby that works. I can see at a glance that I'm connected, which is reassuring. I haven't yet tried it in its router mode, but as a range extender it works great. You need to use the little stowaway stylus that comes with it when you're selecting onscreen functions, but as long as you remember to re-stow it, you've always got it handy if you need it.
text_fidelity_b: Securifi Almond - (3 Minute Setup) Touchscreen Wireless Router/Range Extender

Sony Walkman NWZA17SLV 64 GB Hi-Res Digital Music Player (Silver) I am writing this review because after reading the few reviews available it sounded like this would be a great Media Player. But after receiving the player (a Christmas gift from my wife) I have to wonder if most of the people who reviewed the unit have actually used or even seen one in person. So I reread the reviews and noticed a trend that they don't actually say anything about using the player (all except one).
So here is a real user review.
The good. (I use it for music playback only)
The sound on the player is superb. I rip my cd's using the FLAC format and I have listed to playback using Wired (Grado's) and Bluetooth headphones. I have also listened to it on my home stereo using wired and a Bluetooth connection. There is a slight difference in the tonal quality but in a noisy environment my ears can't tell the difference. Sony digital processor does seem to color the music a little but it is on the warm side so it not objectionable.
I must say I love the sound of this player.
The media program (Media Go) that comes with it is very good for ripping music in any format that the player supports. Setting up playlist to send to the player is a breeze. The program does not have the options of JRiver Media Center but it is simpler to use.
The Bad
It is cheaply built - If feels like a toy. I do not believe it will stand up to daily use. Not a quality product that I have come to expect from Sony. For the price of this unit I expect it to at least have the build quality of my FiiO player or my cassette Walkman (which still works)
Bluetooth- It's a joke. My main reason of wanting this player was Bluetooth connectivity. If you disconnect it from the headphones, stereo -car and home, It take at least three tries for it to reconnect the next time you want to use it and you have to navigate to the Bluetooth screen to do it.
This creates a problem on its own. If you were listening to your playlist and stop at a particular track you now loose that place unless you navigate back to the home screen (more on that later) and bookmark your spot before you try and reconnect to your Bluetooth playback source. This is a major pain.
Screen Navigation. The player has 4 main buttons. The toggle button which surrounds the play and pause button is use for navigation. The navigation is more cumbersome -not user friendly- than it needs to be. Try and navigate while you are working out or somewhere not so well lit and it is frustrating at best. At this price it should have a touch screen. My 29 dollar SanDisk player is easier to use that this setup.
The next problem. You really can't power down the player. Once you power down the player if you accidently touch any button on the player it powers back up. I keep the player in a soft case clipped to my belt. I have bumped the player while in the case and have ended up with a dead battery the next time I wanted to use it.
There are other problems but they are minor and I can live with those.
If Sony wants to play in this market (no pun intended) these major flaws need to be fixed.
Tried to post a review on Sony's web site and they would not let it post. So I don't trust any reviews on their web site at this point. This is why I am posting it here to at least let potential buyers be aware of what it is really like to use this player.
text_fidelity_b: Sony Walkman NWZA17SLV 64 GB Hi-Res Digital Music Player (Silver)

text_fidelity_a: JBL On Tour Portable Speaker System ( Black ) This is a great, little device!  First of all, I think it's beautiful and sleek, and easy to use.  Just slide it open, plug in the cable that links to your iPod, and if you are using batteries, that's it, good to go.  Just plug in the AC cord if you aren't using batteries.  Uses 4 AAA batteries, so the batteries are small, don't add any noticeable weight to the unit.  Your iPod stays in it's own protective case, no fitting it onto a dock slot.  I've had one Altec Lansing speaker set and one Sonic Impact speaker set that the slot became damaged, so I'm glad I don't deal with that anymore.  This thing is light, small, about the size of a very, VERY large eyeglasses case so it packs very nicely in a purse, carry-on or suitcase, even better if you can get along without the bulky AC cord and just use batteries.  But it's about the sound, isn't it?  If you are looking for sound in your hotel room, or bathroom, mobile home, bedroom, kitchen, garage, den, etc., you are going to LOVE this little guy, and it will be more than loud enough, it can crank!  The sound is really great!  It looks great, performs great, and I just bought another one for a friend going to Mexico in a week.  Now, if you want a loud, space-filling but still portable speaker, get the In-Motion IM9 unit, as I did also.  I have both.  The IM9 is too big for the suitcase, and it's REALLY heavy, but it's screaming loud, great for the backyard or tailgating or any party setting, and very compact and portable while protecting the iPod within it's great loading system.  But this JBL is your OTHER speaker system for light weight travel or just to fill a room at home.  If you don't love it as I do, I don't know what planet you live on!

text_fidelity_a:
MOSISO Fashion Laptop Backpack for Women, Pure Deep Gray I am in love with this bag!
It has so many features that are important to me.
I plan on using this bag for day trips with the family and especially during my childrens' swim meets.
This bag has more compartments and zippers then I expected it to have.
There are three main large compartments, two small compartments in the front and an anti-theft pocket in the back and the side water bottle mesh are also contained in a pocket. I was a little worried that I wouldn't be able to fit my water bottle in the outside mesh since there is a zipper and extra fabric and stuff, but as you can see from my image, a sports drink bottle fits perfectly in there.
The bag comes with its own lock which can be programmed to your own code.
The bag has two padded sections within the two largest zippered areas. One for a laptop with a velcro strip and one in the middle section with no velcro.
I plan to use the middle padded area for my mp3 player as this is the area that the headphone cables enter into and I will also put my power bank in that padded area since this is also where the charger port comes from.
The color of this bag is very modern, it's a good bag for a male or female.
I like that I can zip shut the drink compartments if I wanted to have something in them that I don't want to fall out (skittles/sunflower seeds)!
There is a padded carry handle and a non-padded hanging handle which is really nice. The back is very padded as are the shoulder straps.
There is even a luggage strap for if I wanted to bring this on the plane trip.
There are two cinch straps above each water bottle which is nice, as sometimes I like to cinch in my jacket or if I had a lot of bulky stuff inside that could be cinched to remove air and the bulk.
The bag has the interior organization in the front large compartment, including a clip for your keys, two wider sections, mesh on one and two pencil holes, which is great for me as I like to bring a pencil, sharpie, and highlighter with me to the swim meets.
I like that there are so many large compartments, allowing me to keep my stuff separate. I like to bring magazines to read between heats and sometimes my laptop (rear), snacks in the middle and the schedule and journal in the front.
I like the smaller compartment to contain the emergency kit (bandaids, pain reliever, etc).
I don't think there is anything else in a bag that this bag doesn't have.
A great mom bag!
text_fidelity_b: MOSISO Fashion Laptop Backpack for Women, Pure Deep Gray

text_fidelity_a:
Sony STRDH190 2-ch Home Stereo Receiver with Phono Inputs & Bluetooth Black While I might give this product four stars for being so basic and catering to the "just playing music off my phone" crowd, you can't argue with a product done right. And actually, for those who just play music off their phones, this is a huge step up from some Bluetooth speaker that so many people seem to have resorted to.

Basically, if you want a decent stereo for a room with no TV and you don't want to stream over the network (yes, you can do it through your phone, but that seems onerous at best), this is likely the stereo for you.

I like the Sony heft and quality, as well as classic design. I like that it has quite a few inputs including one with ground, and that it has an aux-in port in the front.

I love that you can do two sets of speakers, if you want to fill a large room evenly or if you want to cover two areas independently. You can also change from speaker A to speaker B to A+B to off via the remote, which my higher end 7.1 Sony stereo's remote cannot do (and that is annoying).

This is about perfect for my workshop (no TV, Internet streaming device nearby to give a physical output).

Speaker terminals are the cheaper-than-usual-for-Sony spring loaded type instead of 5-way posts. This is the least-premium feature of this stereo. No AM radio if you care.

I would sort of like an Ethernet interface, but properly accessing it without an external screen (which would require a video output that this receiver doesn't have) would be limiting.

Personally, I hate Bluetooth in this application, especially via phone, because you move to another room, the connection dies. I know a lot of people get through their lives with just the music on their phones, but there's always a better way. If you have one of those setups where you have a music player hooked to this and you can control that with your phone, that would be a pretty good setup.

Beautiful and robust receiver at a low price point if you don't aspire for other options. Great for a workshop or other TV-less space.
text_fidelity_b: Sony STRDH190 2-ch Home Stereo Receiver with Phono Inputs & Bluetooth Black

text_fidelity_a:
ZUGU CASE - 2019 iPad Air 10.5/2017 iPad Pro 10.5 inch Case Prodigy X - Very Protective But Thin + Convenient Magnetic Stand + Sleep/Wake Cover (Purple) Update: A good pencil sleeve to use with this case after stretching it out a bit with a crayola dry erase marker is the Hydream Silicone Case for Apple Pencil Holder Sleeve Skin Pocket Cover Accessories for iPad Pro 9.7/10.5/12.9, Cute Soft Grip Pouch with Charging Cap Holder and 2 Protective Nib Covers.

TL:DR - a fantastic case and looks amazing with a screen protector on the device. Does not interfere with screen protectors at all. Great utility and angle options. Looks good on the fridge too. If you don't mind the case feeling a bit awkward to hold when looking at things in portrait and the fact that your Pencil Sleeve options are limited due to the super tight elastic (I used a crayola dry eraser to stretch mine and now the fit perfect) this is the case for you.

Pros:
8 Adjustment points
The packaging and info included on the company
The quality
The looks (at least in black for me)
The pencil sleeve built in
The wake/sleep utility
Solid positions minus the last one if you're really pretty on it. Like heavy handed drawing hard.

Cons:
The tablet is hard to hold in portrait especially if the pencil is in the case
I know the 2018 Pro model had yet to be released when this case was made, but I wish the placement of the Pencil sleeve was in a better location or allowed enough space for a wider variety of pencil sleeves. It makes me worry that it sticks out a little from the case. Kinda wish it was on the top or had a similar elastic sleeve loop on the top where an Apple Pencil 2 would sit magnetically. More or a nitpick though.
The tightness of the sleeve out of the box! This was very annoying, but another nitpick since I can always stretch it out.
A little awkward to use the rear-facing camera since when holding with the front panel touching the back of the case it covers the camera completely. Even when in landscape you have to tilt it high enough to free your view.

Quality of Life Cons: (basically super nitpicks. Feel free to ignore. The case is great!)
Would have been nice if they added another small sleeve near the rear pencil sleeve for the small charging Pencil dongle. It looks like there is enough room in the back.
Like the little indents where the power and volume buttons are located I'd have liked to see a little notch above the charging port center of the charging port. Why? Because I often find myself inserting the connector low of the actual charging port and a little notch where the middle would generally be would have been a nice touch or at least some more material to alleviate confusion on the port's location. If you look at the charging port with the case on you'll see what I mean, there is a little lip which can make it confusing on what I'm inserting the plug into (done this a lot lately, but getting better at it).
A somewhat more rigid hinge on the panel that covers the screen. Why? It can get really floppy when holding it in portrait mode and a slightly more rigid hinge kind of like the surface pro keyboard cover would have been nice. The panel itself is solid but the material connecting it to the case can be a little floppy.
text_fidelity_b: ZUGU CASE - 2019 iPad Air 10.5/2017 iPad Pro 10.5 inch Case Prodigy X - Very Protective But Thin + Convenient Magnetic Stand + Sleep/Wake Cover (Purple)

Sony Cyber-shot DSC-H55 14.1MP Digital Camera with 10x Wide Angle Optical Zoom with SteadyShot Image Stabilization and 3.0 inch LCD (Black) (Discontinued by Manufacturer) Sony Cyber-shot DSC -H 55.
I have owned two other cameras in the past. My last Camera, before this one, was a 12 Megapixel. And I thought it, at first to be ALL THAT. This was only because my previous camera had been a four Megapixel. I was so impressed with the increase in the resolution that is all I could see was the ability to crop photos to a better end then I had been able to. After the newness had worn off I began to realize the Cameron was just a lemon. So with this camera, that mistake will not happen again. The (14 Megapixel) of this Sony camera is not that different from my (12 Megapixel) camera that I am replacing. So I will look past the resolution difference with ease.
However the (10 x) zoom lens is NEW. Not only to me, but to all (point and shoot) cameras I have ever seen. Now, the 10 x zoom lens that I am talking about is NOT digital zoom. But rather, purely optical. There is a digital zoom offered in the menus of this camera. But I simply turned this feature off. If I want to do any digital zoom, I'll do it in Photoshop on my own time.
Other perks include; a battery and charger. The battery is lithium. And knowing that a lithium battery must be conditioned before its true capacity can ever be obtained. And even before the battery had been `conditioned' it was still able to take approximately 400 shots. And of course four or five HRS of me playing around in the menus with the features. And I know from past experience this can be one of the biggest power drains on a camera battery. And this is only the first cycle. I don't foresee a need in my future to buy a spear battery.
While I am on the subject of batteries, I need to mention. The battery charger is a cute little thing. The part of the plug that actually goes into the wall will fold into the plastic housing. So it is not a burdensome piece of machinery to store. And the whole thing is extremely small. It is only 3"x2"x1". To me that sounds ridiculously small, and if it were not right here in front of me I might not even believe. But it is true. It will fit in my small camera case, instead of the drawer. I already have enough mess around my room.
Also about batteries, there is a handy little gauge, on the LCD screen, that reports the amount of battery left by a four bar indicator (like a cell phone).
I spoke earlier about the massive zoom lens. But I didn't even tell how this camera can also take a macro picture up to about 8" away at full wide angle (zoom out). The 8" I just spoke could be off a little by + or - an inch. The manual that could tell me for sure is over there in that box, and I am over here. And I'm a lazy person.
I'm really impressed at how small this camera is. It will fit very nicely, with lots of room to spare, in my chest pocket. I do wear a 2X shirt, but there is so much room left over, I bet you could fit this camera in a large size pocket. I haven't had a chance to test it; I'm just using my best estimate. On outings, being able to tuck this camera away in my pocket will be way awesome. And it is so light weight.
And it weighs very, very little for such a nice camera. I have a cordless optical mouse hooked up to this computer. So by comparing weight, the mouse is the more heavy of the two.
I think I have touched on the biggest topics I can think of at this sitting, but to sum this up. This is the best camera I (personally) have ever owned. This would include 2 other digital cameras (one SLR type & one point and shoot) and a couple `film cameras' 110 and a 35mm SLR my uncle left to me. And after comparing it with all the other ones available at the stores, it IS the best. I compare every time a store has a display, to see if mine is still better. Even some of the `better' SLR types that sell for $100's, fall short. I would be really upset to see that a little `point & shoot' can beat my $800 `SLR type' camera.
At $225 and $25 3 year extended warranty from Samsclub, I have a new gizmo and I did not break the bank.
text_fidelity_b: Sony Cyber-shot DSC-H55 14.1MP Digital Camera with 10x Wide Angle Optical Zoom with SteadyShot Image Stabilization and 3.0 inch LCD (Black) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

ARRIS® Surfboard® SB6190 Cable Modem, White We used the SB6120 modem & D-Link DIR-825 router for many years. We kept track of speeds and issues for those years and noticed speeds had not improved (even though our service did) and more issues were coming up as our neighborhood is growing and more people are getting cable. After much research we decided to upgrade our whole home network. We wanted to get the best we could afford so we chose this [[ASIN:B016PE1X5K ARRIS SURFboard SB6190 DOCSIS 3.0 Cable Modem]], the [[ASIN:B00BUSDVBQ TP-LINK Archer C7 AC1750 Dual Band Wireless AC Gigabit Router, 2.4GHz 450Mbps+5Ghz 1300Mbps, 2 USB Ports, IPv6, Guest Network]], and the [[ASIN:B00A121WN6 TP-LINK 8-Port Gigabit Ethernet Desktop Switch (TL-SG108)]]. We knew we would get better speeds, but wow!

We have had Cox (Phoenix) Premier 100 Mbps / 10 Mbps for the last 13 years or so.

Old Equipment Comparisons (1st # is download speed, 2nd # is upload speed, 3rd is latency)
11/25/2011 12:35 PM MST 29.40 Mb/s 12.62 Mb/s 30 ms
6/20/2012 1:11 PM MST 32.95 Mb/s 14.47 Mb/s 33 ms
8/4/2014 11:11 AM MST 37.64 Mb/s 12.48 Mb/s 12 ms
Today, after setting up all the new stuff test results were much, much better (see pics).
6/20/2016 8:18 PM MST 169.67 Mb/s 12.27 Mb/s 32 ms

We were a bit nervous at first, seeing that some reviews said these modems don't work with Cox (even though their website says it does). But it works with Cox just fine. I think it's possible that people that had issues either 1) got a lemon (that can and does happen with everything, so although a pain, it shouldn't be a determining factor), or 2) the cable company employee helping them didn't know what they were doing.

Now to go download stuff just to see how fast it finishes. :)
