PYvideo Backup Camera Kit for Toyota Camry SE and XLE (2012-2014) for Factory Display (Color: Black) I'm writing this review in 2023 and I've owned the 2013 Camry SE since it was new. I wish I'd installed this years ago.

Having a backup camera is certainly not a necessity, but installing this one was incredibly easy, and it functions great. The kit I received came with the orange trunk tab tool, so I didn't even need any specialized tools. It required a set of wire cutters, some electrical tape, a 5/16" drill bit with drill,

The whole process of installing the camera took me about an hour and would have taken probably much less time if I were more mechanically inclined. For my particular model of Camry (2013 SE), there was already a plug in just sitting there for a backup camera and this kit came with the camera, the cord that passes from the trunk to the console and the specialized plug. I didn't even have to disassemble the radio.

Now, when I shift into reverse, it just works!!

I'm sure that more modern cameras have even better resolution, but this one works great for parallel parking or for reversing out in a busy parking lot.

I'm thankful for YouTube for making theses projects feel do-able. I made use of a video called "2012 to 2014 Camry SE & XLE rear view camera installation" posted by "Repairs by C-Top."

AmazonBasics Vehicle Power Cable with Mini-USB Connector for GPS and Other Mini-USB Devices This cord is marketed as a direct replacement to the Garmin power cord. That's why I purchased it. And though it features the compact right angle mini USB plug on one end and provides adequate power to run my 2505LMT, when I plug the cord into the Garmin it immediately reports that the traffic function will not work.

Upon closer examination of the OEM power coed, I observe that it has a blivet on the cord near the 12v plug end that must be the traffic receiver.

This cord has no such receiver and cannot help the 2595LMT receive traffic information.

On the other hand, most of the time traffic information is bogus. And more annoying than useful. The Garmin is constantly binging at me to take an alternate route that never is a better route.

Today I tried following its suggestion to get off the freeway in LA because the Garmin was concerned that the freeway was clogged. It told me to take La Cienega to save 4 minutes. Ha. La Cienega was much, much worse than the freeway and ended up costing me 15 minutes or more. (I think it assumes no one is using surface streets in LA in morning rush hour traffic--a fatal assumption.

Later in the trip it told me the freeway was closed ahead and to take an alternate route. I didn't believe it as I could see with my eyes and the excellent traffic flow in both directions that there was no actual blockage.

So, if you don't mind not having the traffic function, this cord works fine. (And since I don't trust the traffic function, I'll probably turn it off my self -- regardless of cord used.)
text_fidelity_b: AmazonBasics Vehicle Power Cable with Mini-USB Connector for GPS and Other Mini-USB Devices

Nikon D810 FX-format Digital SLR Camera Body I have had this camera since July 2015 and I find that this camera to be the most incredible camera I have ever owned. I have owned the D700, D800, D600, D610 and still own the D750.The clarity and dynamic range surpasses all of my previous cameras, including my D750.
However, the D810 is very demanding on lenses. Inferior lenses will provide either inconsistent performance, or just plain horrendous results.
Edit: 11/29/2017: After over two years of regular use I have had no problems with this camera. I have never had to clean my sensor, and I change lenses frequently, as I most often use prime lenses. So, I don’t understand why so many people have the need to frequently to “dust off” or clean their sensor. Nor do I understand why some people complain about the fact that most of the outer shell is made of carbon fiber. For years I worked with advanced composites, and carbon fiber is not just cheap plastic, but is used in many high-tech products for its superior strength and light weight.
I can only speak from my own experience and knowledge.
text_fidelity_b: Nikon D810 FX-format Digital SLR Camera Body

text_fidelity_a:
HP 970 Programmable Wireless Keyboard (Silver) - Bluetooth & 2.4 GHz Wireless Multi-Device Connectivity - USB-C Rechargeable Battery - 24 Programmable Keys - Works with Windows & MacOS (3Z729AA#ABA) I got my first PC in 2003, and had a corded mouse. Looking back, I can BARELY remember the mouse that came with that Gateway PC. In 2004, my mom bought a Dell PC and traded me for my Gateway – don’t judge, she just wanted something to browse the internet and play games on.

Between 2003-2005, I used an awkward racecar shaped mouse, but went back to the more streamlined corded mouse for my desktops.

In 2005, when I got a laptop, I got my first wireless mouse and liked it. It was a Logitech.

By 2010, I got my first HP laptop – and as usual, got a specific mouse for it, again Logitech. The reason? My hand. I don’t have very big hands and hate to “splay” my fingers out trying to grip the mouse. That continued with a backup laptop in 2011 with some college money.

I even got “backup” mice, I just LOVED the Logitech ones.

Last year, 2021, I got another HP laptop for my birthday and yes – a “Logi” mouse (M317 – Amazon code B08L8SRJRR; white with purple/pink side grip, flowers on top). This was a bit smaller than my previous mice. But, I love it.

Thinking this might be a bit better – I got it.

Right off – it is a bit “extra”. I can BARELY grip it to get it to do what I need to do. The “thumb” rest was a good idea, the USB rechargeable feature was nice, programmable buttons – a bit beyond me. This is definitely for someone who needs those features.

As far as “quiet” with regards to the scrolling and clicking – I don’t see the need for the feature. When I’m typing on they keyboard that is noisier than my mouse.

It was response and fast – but not enough to justify a purchase of it.

It connects the same way my “Logi” does – USB dongle. Both mice take ONE (1) AA battery

At the current price of $67.52 – this is a definitely no-go for me.
text_fidelity_b: HP 970 Programmable Wireless Keyboard (Silver) - Bluetooth & 2.4 GHz Wireless Multi-Device Connectivity - USB-C Rechargeable Battery - 24 Programmable Keys - Works with Windows & MacOS (3Z729AA#ABA)

text_fidelity_a:
Kindle Oasis E-reader (Previous Generation - 9th) – Graphite, 7" High-Resolution Display (300 ppi), Waterproof, Built-In Audible, 32 GB, Wi-Fi - with Special Offers (Closeout) I purchased one of these 9th generation Kindle Oasis. The first unit I received would freeze during the configuration process. You could reset it, but if you try to configure, it would freeze again. At this point, I made the mistake of asking for a replacement instead of just returning the faulty Kindle Oasis for a refund. A replacement unit arrived in three days. Unfortunately, the replacement unit was DoA. There was a fixed image on screen, and I wasn't able to get a response from this Kindle after charging it for a long time and multiple reset attempts. I had already shipped the first unit back using a UPS shipping label created by Amazon at this point. I went to my Amazon Orders page to return the second unit for a credit. But Amazon web interface wouldn't allow a self service return for refund. I had contact customer service and deal with several customer service representatives. They consistently asked me to try some simple trouble shooting steps ( most of which are not even applicable if you have a completely dead kindle). They wouldn't listen to me when I said I just wanted to return it, and try to pressure me into another replacement. At this point, I had spent several hours troubleshooting, talking to Amazon Customer service, taking packages to UPS, etc. so I insisted on a return for refund. This time, the customer service representative said he was having problems generating the return label, and then disappeared. After several minutes of wait, another customer rep took over and worked on this case for another 10 minutes or so. At that point, I ended up with two sets of return labels in my email. The customer service rep told me to use the labels from the second email (in chronological order). So the next day, I shipped the replacement Kindle Oasis back. A few days later, I saw on UPS tracking that the package was delivered to Amazon and three days after this I received an email confirmation from Amazon that my first return was received. A few days later, I saw on UPS tracking that the second Kindle Oasis (replacement) was also received by Amazon. I waited a few days for return confirmation and refund from Amazon, but nothing happened. When I contacted Amazon Customer service, they kept telling me that I shouldn't worry about getting charged as my replacement is complete. But they could see no record of my return of the replacement. I spent probably a good half an hour chatting with a customer service rep but they couldn't help me at all since they could only see the record for on return request. That chat ended with no resolution because I ran out of time and had to get to an appointment. Later, I got in touch with yet another service rep, and explained everything from scratch. Luckily, that person was able to find records of both returns being received by Amazon and finally issued me a refund.

So lessons from this story:
1. Don't buy a 9th gen Kindle Oasis. There seems to be serious quality control issues. The probability of one customer receiving two faulty Kindles in a row would be infinitesimal unless fault rates are in the 20% range.
2. If you receive a faulty Kindle from Amazon, return it for a refund. Don't ask for a replacement. Amazon's automated return process cannot handle the return of a replacement unit, and you will sink a lot of time dealing with customer service representatives
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Oasis E-reader (Previous Generation - 9th) – Graphite, 7" High-Resolution Display (300 ppi), Waterproof, Built-In Audible, 32 GB, Wi-Fi - with Special Offers (Closeout)

Dell Premier Slim Backpack 14 This laptop backpack is suitable for both genders and all ages, but a busy business traveler might appreciate it most of all, because it is fancy enough to bring to a high-class business meeting. The backpack is padded and well made out of matte-black, water-resistant, "pu leather." This is poly-synthetic leather, which mostly looks and feels like real leather, though it is much less durable than real leather and isn't as thick. It certainly is more water resistant than real leather, so that is an advantage, and it also costs less than leather.

There are pockets for organizing various items, and the laptop sleeve is plush lined to protect a laptop from banging. There is also padding on the back side of the pack to cushion your back from sharp edges, which is an excellent comfort-inducing addition to the design. The zipper closure is high quality and should resist snagging and breaking.

All in all, this is a high quality backpack for those who prefer not to carry an old-fashioned briefcase.
text_fidelity_b: Dell Premier Slim Backpack 14

text_fidelity_a:
Philips SHQ3200BK/28 ActionFit Sports Earhook Headphones While they are ok for the price in terms of sound quality, fit, and durability, they lack a fundamental function for what Many people use to play their music: the ability to receive and make phone calls. If you are using a smartphone, these are only headphones, not headphones with a function button (like the kind that come with an iPhone, for example), and not ones that have an output through which you can speak or take dictation.
That aside, the sound quality was ok, with a somewhat tinny, canned quality and poor capability in processing deep bass or treble. If changing the levels to decrease treble, you'll see some improvement in the sound. For anything spoken word like podcasts, these are fine.
The fit is not bad. Usually, these things are big on me (female with apparently small ear-holes, if you would judge by most headphones), but these were comfortable. The three sizes of rubbery earplugs always help and are generally standard, and the ear hooks also aide in keeping them in place.

Summary:
For the price, you get decent headphones that do not have an output function.

TP-Link Deco Mesh WiFi System(Deco M5) –Up to 5,500 sq. ft. Whole Home Coverage and 100+ Devices,WiFi Router/Extender Replacement, Anitivirus, 3-pack This review is for the TP-LInk Mesh WiFi M5 system.
—————
Amended April 28, 2020
Now that I’ve been using this for a couple weeks, I am returning to add these units HAVE NOT cured the dead spots that needed more signal strength. Yes, the WiFi signal is present in those areas of my home. However, the signal strength has not improved over what my centrally located router produced on its own. Essentially for my roughly $125, I got a couple stylish WiFi access points. What I DID NOT GET is the improved coverage promoted in the description.
—————
This IS NOT a plug it in and it works system. You need to know at minimum:
—Your current router’s IP address, the user ID for it, and the password. If you haven’t changed them from the default, you have no business installing a network anything, because you put EVERYTHING on your system at high risk for hacking. Why? The problem is that the default user ID and password are the SAME FOR ALL routers of the same brand (every brand router has a published default user id and password).
—You need to know which of several comm protocols your ISP uses.
—You need to know that IF YOU SWAP OUT YOUR ROUTER for one of the units, the others WILL NOT WORK to extend your WiFi network. For that you need to set these up as extenders, with the first being connected to your existing router.
—To set up a network of WiFi extenders, you need to know how to turn your existing router’s WiFi transmission off. Only then can you use these as extenders, satellites, or whatever you know them as.
—You are highly likely to have to update the firmware on each M5 device.
—You should set aside about two to three hours to set up a network of multiple devices.
—If you set these up as extenders, some of the default security features are switched off. You need to be sure these security features are enabled on your router instead.

I found this an unacceptably under-documented product that forces you to comb through the internet for proper setup tips. I loathe their little booklet that is “documentation” since it is a collection of single pages in multiple languages that direct you to the App Store or Google Play for the app that manages setup. That app is underpowered, has little relevant or helpful information.

I’ve been working with and installing systems from early (1990s) mainframes, Apple IIs, Macs, PCs of all flavors, and networks right up to now. Were it not for that experience, I might never have gotten this to work. Once installed, it works fine.

Recommendation: If your current router is older, you’re probably more likely to get better WiFi coverage by purchasing a newer, more current router. Try that first, and if you don't get the coverage you need, add a couple or three of these.
text_fidelity_b: TP-Link Deco Mesh WiFi System(Deco M5) –Up to 5,500 sq. ft. Whole Home Coverage and 100+ Devices,WiFi Router/Extender Replacement, Anitivirus, 3-pack

CORSAIR Hydro Series H105 AIO Liquid CPU Cooler, 240mm Thick Radiator, Dual 120mm PWM Fans I've wanted to try one of these liquid CPU coolers for ages, but it always been a little too cheap to spend the extra money on one, and I confess I've been mildly concerned about using a liquid anything inside my computer. I'm glad I tried this out.

This particular model has a radiator style grate which the fan sits on (there is some conductive paste included), then has tubes leading to the cooler unit. The water is totally enclosed in the system, and I can see no danger of leakage. The fan is quiet and unobtrusive.

It has a four pin connector, so if your computer has a four pin connector as well, your computer can control the speed of the fan. However, the four pin connector can also connect to a three pin connector and it works fine, you just lose that extra bit of control.

The one small improvement I'd like to see is that the water/cooling area only goes to one side of the radiator type grate, not around all of the edges, so one side of it will always be hotter than the other. It still disperses heat well, just seems like a less efficient system then it could be.

Lastly, I love the thumbscrews included for installing. I hate dealing with normal screws, and the thumbscrews are such a thoughtful touch that it made me think well of the company for including them.

Overall, if you've been on the fence about testing out one of these new liquid CPU coolers, I don't see any reason not to try out this one. The price is reasonable for what it is, and it looks like a highly effective setup, certainly better than just using a fan.
text_fidelity_b: CORSAIR Hydro Series H105 AIO Liquid CPU Cooler, 240mm Thick Radiator, Dual 120mm PWM Fans

text_fidelity_a:
Roku Express - HD Streaming Player It may not be a techie's delight, but if you are looking for a budget streaming device, this one fits the bill. First off it is quite small making it ideal for cramped or limited spaces like a vacation home or boat. It comes with a short, two foot long cable and a piece of two sided tape. It connects to your tv with the cable.Depending where you tv is located you might have to use a longer cable. I did and found that the tape is not just a nice idea, it is a necessity. the box is so small and most cables so rigid it flips the box off making it impossible to regulate with the infrared remote. Take time to position because while the tape adheres well it looses its stickiness after being removed and repositioned. The infrared remote must be in line of sight for it to work. The way around that is to use the app. The app works with both android and iOS. The app has a voice control which I found to be inconsistent and a private listening feature that lets you use your phone headphones and mute the TV.

Performance is mixed. navigating and launching is slow. Netflix in particular really dragged. but playing content was excellent with no lag or problems. the channel selection is good with pretty much everything you would want available.

This is not bad for a budget streamer. there are definitely downsides, the ir remote, the lack of speed, the need for a cable. but it does work and is small enough for travel. I am frequently on the road for business and this does expand the limited options of hotel televisions. If you are on a budget and don't need or want the features that are available on pricier models this low end streamer will get the job done.
text_fidelity_b: Roku Express - HD Streaming Player

text_fidelity_a: Mediabridge™ HDMI Cable (6 Feet) Supports 4K@60Hz, High Speed, Hand-Tested, HDMI 2.0 Ready - UHD, 18Gbps, Audio Return Channel In past days I bought into a lot of the HYPE from non-manufacturer's like MONSTER CABLE that their overly expensive HDMI-ETC. cables including HDMI are worth the price. A digital signal especially for anything less than 25 orr 30 feet is a digital signal and as long as the cable is connected to the HDMI ends you get the same quality of 0/1 as you do with a ridiculously priced cable. I ordered both HDMI and Fiber Toslink cables from this branded manufacturer and they came packaged nicely and safely to prevent damage in transit with the UPS monsters and are performing perfectly. I actually did pay over $50.00 for a six-foot HDMI cable at Best Buy and all I can say is that I must have had a lot of money to waste as this brand is equally as reliable and I could have purchased twenty of these for the price of the one Monster at Best Buy. The only people who will argue these points are snobs who think there is some sort of prestige associated with having over priced digital cables. If this was for speakers or other copper reliant products I would at least partially agree that high-quality is very important but even there we are still getting products shipped mainly from China that have the fancy packaging and marketing hype attached to them and you can do a lot better shopping for solid quality without all the needless BS. But these and you will be pleased. SS
text_fidelity_b: Mediabridge™ HDMI Cable (6 Feet) Supports 4K@60Hz, High Speed, Hand-Tested, HDMI 2.0 Ready - UHD, 18Gbps, Audio Return Channel
